entries.name: NETSUITE_ACCOUNT_ID
entries.description: The NetSuite account id, as NetSuite writes it: digits, with _SB1 or the like for a sandbox.
howToGet: The account id is the first part of the account's SuiteTalk host, such as 1234567 in 1234567.suitetalk.api.netsuite.com, as NetSuite's SuiteQL guide shows. A sandbox host writes _SB1 as -sb1.

entries.name: NETSUITE_CLIENT_ID
entries.description: The client id of the integration record made for KaratOS, with the client credentials (machine-to-machine) grant and only the REST web services scope.
howToGet: An administrator creates an integration record with the client credentials (machine-to-machine) grant and only the REST web services scope, as NetSuite's OAuth 2.0 client credentials guide describes.
Copy the client id it shows. The client secret isn't needed.

entries.name: NETSUITE_CERTIFICATE_ID
entries.description: The certificate id NetSuite gives when the administrator maps KaratOS's certificate to the integration record, a role that can only view, and an entity.
howToGet: Make a role that can only view: items, vendors, the transactions read (sales orders, purchase orders, invoices, journal entries), and locations, with the REST Web Services and Log in using OAuth 2.0 Access Tokens permissions, and nothing that creates or edits.
An administrator maps the certificate to the integration record, that role and an entity, as NetSuite's client credentials guide describes, and copies the certificate id NetSuite gives.

entries.name: NETSUITE_PRIVATE_KEY
entries.description: The private key of the certificate mapped for KaratOS: RSA of 3072 or 4096 bits, or EC on P-256, P-384 or P-521. It signs each sign-in and is never sent anywhere. As PEM, or base64-encoded on one line.
howToGet: Make a key pair and a certificate for it, valid for at most two years, and give the administrator only the certificate to map.
Copy the private key straight into the host's secret store, as PEM or base64-encoded on one line. Never paste it into chat or an issue.
